title: EASTCOAST Half Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2025 Race Was Like
seo_title: EASTCOAST Half Marathon Review: Kuantan Course, Weather, Cut-offs
meta_description: EASTCOAST Half Marathon review: the first edition on 7 December 2025, from Jalan Besar to Benteng Kuantan, 24°C and humid at the 4am start, a four-hour cut-off and six water stations.
dek: What the first EASTCOAST Half Marathon in Kuantan was like in December 2025: the old-town start and the finish by Menara 188, the warm, humid pre-dawn start, the cut-offs and water stations, the size of the field and the race-weekend logistics.
verdict: Enter if you want a small, AIMS-measured half marathon in Kuantan with a forgiving four-hour limit. The first edition, on Sunday 7 December 2025, started on Jalan Besar in the old town and finished at Benteng Kuantan near Menara 188; the organiser thanked 1,470 participants after the race and later put the figure at 1,600. The half marathon started at 4am, closed at 8am and had six water stations. Expect sticky air even before dawn: it was about 24°C at the start with a dew point of 22°C. The organiser has admitted that some stretches were poorly lit because street lights were out. No 2025 results have been found, so this review cannot say how fast the field was.

sections.heading: The First Edition: Date, Field and Format
paragraphs: The 2025 EASTCOAST Half Marathon was on Sunday 7 December 2025, organised by Elpis Event Management, with a 4am start and Menara 188 in Kuantan given as the venue [1]. It was the race's first edition [5]. After the race the organiser thanked 1,470 participants [5]; in October 2026 it gave the 2025 figure as 1,600 participants [6]. Neither post splits the field by distance.

There were five events: a 21.1 km half marathon and a 10 km, each with an open category for ages 18 to 39 and a veteran category for 40 to 70; a 5 km fun run, with a separate boys' and girls' category for ages 13 to 17; a 1.5 km kids' dash for ages 6 to 12; and a family walk for groups of three [1]. The half marathon and 10 km carried timing chips, only half marathoners received a finisher tee, and every category got an event tee, a medal and an e-certificate [4]. Prizes went to the top five in each half-marathon and 10 km category and in the 5 km and 1.5 km boys' and girls' races [1].

The organiser named BMAI Malaysia, Coros Malaysia, KMI Kuantan Medical Centre, BigBigPlace, MedgelX and 100PLUS as its main sponsors and Menara 188 Kuantan as event partner, and described the race as a 'runcation' meant to bring visitors to Kuantan, in line with its commitment to Tourism Pahang [5].

sections.heading: The Course: From Jalan Besar to Benteng Kuantan
paragraphs: The start line was on Jalan Besar, in front of Café 1940, which the organiser chose as a symbol of the old buildings of Kuantan town; the finish was at Benteng Kuantan, near Menara 188 [5].

The organiser says the half-marathon and 10 km courses were AIMS-certified, making this the first race in Kuantan to receive that recognition [5]. The Ticket2u page did not carry a half-marathon route map, saying the course would be published once AIMS certification came through; it describes the route only as passing the town's streets, historic landmarks and well-known spots [1].

The published 10 km route profile shows a single loop from the start that crosses a bridge marked 'New Bridge' at about 3 km and Jambatan Tanjung Lumpur at about 8 km before returning to the finish, with water stations at 4.2 km and 7.1 km [3].

The organiser's post-race note admits one problem: street lights were not working on several parts of the route, leaving those sections poorly lit, and extra lighting was put up at critical spots during the race [5]. With the half marathon starting at 4am [2], much of it is run before daylight, so the lighting matters more here than at a later-starting race.
The organiser says the 2026 race has a new route [6], so the 2025 course shows the part of town the race uses rather than the exact roads for 2026.

sections.heading: The Weather: Warm, Humid and Dry After a Wet Saturday
paragraphs: Open-Meteo's reanalysis for central Kuantan gives 24.2°C, 88% humidity and a dew point of 22.1°C at the 4am start, under full cloud with a 9 km/h wind [7]. Conditions barely changed over the next four hours: 24.1°C at 6am, 24.0°C at 7am, and 24.5°C with 89% humidity at 8am, when the half marathon closed, by which time cloud cover had thinned to 53% [7].

A dew point above 20°C means sweat evaporates slowly, and the model's apparent ('feels like') temperature was 27.8°C at 4am and 28.3°C at 8am [7]. The heat came later in the morning: the air reached 28.0°C by 10am [7].

The organiser said it had been worried about rain, because it rained heavily all through race-kit collection day and MetMalaysia forecast continuing rain over the weekend; on race morning, it said, the weather was very good, with only light drizzle at about 5am [5]. The reanalysis agrees on the broad picture: 13.7 mm of rain on Saturday 6 December and 0.2 mm on race day [8].

sections.heading: Start Times, Cut-offs and Water Stations
paragraphs: The half marathon started at 4am, with an 8am cut-off and six water stations. The 10 km started at 6.30am and closed at 8.30am, with two water stations; the 5 km started at 7am, and 7.05am for the 13 to 17 category, and closed at 8.30am and 8.35am, with one station; the 1.5 km kids' dash started at 7.45am and the family walk at 7.50am [2].

Four hours for 21.1 km works out to about 11:22 per km, and two hours for 10 km to 12:00 per km, so both limits are within reach of a steady run-walk. Six stations over 21.1 km is one every 3.5 km or so on average, and the race page asked runners to consider carrying their own hydration [1]. The 10 km map places its two stations at 4.2 km and 7.1 km [3].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Race packs were collected on Saturday 6 December from 10am to 5pm; the Ticket2u page listed the venue as to be confirmed [1]. Runners had to bring their official receipt and identity card, and bib transfers were allowed on the same day for a RM30 fee [1].

The organiser took no responsibility for parking problems or for break-ins and vandalism to parked cars, and asked runners to follow the instructions of traffic personnel [1]. For 2026 it recommends staying in central Kuantan near Menara 188, Masjid Negeri Kuantan or Padang MBK 1, which it says are within walking distance of the start line [11].
Entry cost RM100 for the half marathon, RM80 for the 10 km, RM55 for the 5 km, RM45 for the 1.5 km kids' dash and RM150 for a family-walk group of three [2], before Ticket2u's portal fee [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a small, AIMS-measured half marathon on the east coast with a cut-off that suits run-walkers. Expect warm, very humid air from the start, even before dawn, and watch your footing on dark stretches in case the street-lighting problems recur.

The 2026 race is on Sunday 15 November 2026 in Bandar Kuantan [9]. The half marathon again starts at 4am with a four-hour cut-off, now with seven water stations; the 10 km starts at 6.30am with three stations and a two-hour limit, the 5 km at 7.15am and the 1.5 km at 7.45am, and the category sheet carries the World Athletics/AIMS certified-course mark [10]. The organiser reports 2,600 registrations, 1,600 of them in the half marathon, and a new route [6].

Race kits for 2026 are collected at Mana Mana Hall on Saturday 14 November, from 9am to 6pm, on showing an identity card [12]. Klinik As Salam is providing medic runners on the 5 km and 10 km and a medical team at the finish [13], and the pacers are all drawn from the local running community [14].

Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's Ticket2u pages and category sheets, its Instagram posts and Open-Meteo weather reanalysis. No published 2025 results, winners' times or first-hand runner write-ups could be found, so the review says nothing about how fast the field was.

faqs.question: How early does the EASTCOAST Half Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Very early. In 2025 the half marathon started at 4am on Jalan Besar in Kuantan, the 10 km at 6.30am, the 5 km at 7am and the kids' dash at 7.45am. For 15 November 2026 the organiser lists the half marathon at 4am, the 10 km at 6.30am and the 5 km at 7.15am.

faqs.question: What are the cut-offs at the EASTCOAST Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Four hours for the half marathon and two hours for the 10 km. In 2025 the half marathon closed at 8am after a 4am start, about 11:22 per km, and the 10 km closed at 8.30am. The 2026 category sheet keeps the same limits, so a steady run-walk is enough to finish inside them.

faqs.question: How hot and humid is the EASTCOAST Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Warm and very humid, even before dawn. Open-Meteo's reanalysis for Kuantan gives 24.2°C, 88% humidity and a dew point of 22.1°C at the 4am start in 2025, and 24.5°C with 89% humidity at the 8am cut-off. Heavy rain fell the day before, but race morning had only light drizzle.

faqs.question: Where does the EASTCOAST Half Marathon start and finish?
faqs.answer: In central Kuantan. In 2025 the race started on Jalan Besar, outside Café 1940 in the old town, and finished at Benteng Kuantan near Menara 188. The organiser says the 2026 race uses a new route, and it recommends staying near Menara 188, Masjid Negeri Kuantan or Padang MBK 1.

faqs.question: How many runners take part in the EASTCOAST Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: A modest field. After the first edition in December 2025 the organiser thanked 1,470 participants across all five events, and in October 2026 it gave the 2025 figure as 1,600. For 2026 it reports 2,600 registrations, 1,600 of them in the half marathon.

faqs.question: Is the EASTCOAST Half Marathon course certified?
faqs.answer: Yes, according to the organiser. It says the 2025 half-marathon and 10 km courses were AIMS-certified, the first race in Kuantan to receive that recognition, and the 2026 category sheet carries the World Athletics/AIMS certified-course mark. The half-marathon route map was not published on the Ticket2u race page.

editorial_notes: Written 2026-11-06 to the review template, about the previous edition (Sunday 7 December 2025, the first edition, Elpis Event Management). Weather is Open-Meteo reanalysis for the grid point nearest Kuantan (3.83 N, 103.32 E), not a station observation; it shows no rain at 5am, where the organiser reports light drizzle. Participant numbers differ between the organiser's December 2025 post (1,470) and its October 2026 post (1,600); both are given. No official 2025 results were found (checked Ticket2u, the organiser's Instagram, Threads and Facebook, lesgo.my, Howei, JomRun, RaceX Asia and general web searches; CheckPointSpot was behind a bot wall), so no winning times, finisher counts or finish rates are given. The half-marathon route map and water-station positions were not published on the Ticket2u page; the course description uses the 10 km route profile and the organiser's start and finish locations. No runner blogs, Strava write-ups, videos or press reports were found. 2026 kit-collection details are from the organiser's 2 November 2026 notice, which supersedes the 'to be confirmed' venue on the Ticket2u sheet. No rating.
